questions.q: What role did microbes play in shaping Earth's atmosphere?
a: They released oxygen through photosynthesis
They absorbed oxygen from the air
They created the first land plants
They cooled the planet by reflecting light
questions.why: Lesson 1 says microbes were first to use sunlight and released oxygen as a result.

questions.q: How can microbes survive in extreme places?
a: They evolve rapidly and exchange DNA
They hide inside larger animals
They form hard shells around themselves
They stop reproducing entirely
questions.why: Lesson 1 says single-celled microbes can pass DNA to each other and adapt quickly.

questions.q: What happens if your immune system is set too high?
a: It reacts to harmless things and your own cells
It ignores small infections completely
It stops producing antibodies altogether
It becomes resistant to all microbes
questions.why: Lesson 2 compares immunity to a thermostat; too high a setting brings allergies or autoimmune trouble.

questions.q: Why does the summary say children need some exposure to dirt?
a: It helps calibrate the immune system
It teaches them to avoid germs
It replaces the need for vaccines
It builds resistance to every disease
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the right amount of microbial exposure tunes the immune system, especially in childhood.

questions.q: What was the RePOOPulate project used for?
a: Transplanting healthy stool to treat infection
Engineering bacteria that glow when antibiotics appear
Producing yogurt with extra live probiotic cultures
Sterilizing hospital rooms more effectively
questions.why: Lesson 3 says donated healthy samples were transplanted to fight Clostridium difficile.
